texts.facts: The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road accident dated 20.06.2022. 2. Due to this accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he suffered permanent disablement as such till Mallikarjuna .G.A vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93094840/ 2 now unable to report to duty. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA04C9547 and the Vijayanagara Traffic police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.0066/2022 punishable u/Sec.279, 338 of IPC. The 1st Respondent being the Insurer and the 2 nd respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, this petition. In spite of due service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appear. The driver of the Tempo Traveler did not possess valid DL as on the date of accident and the vehicular documents such as FC and Permit are also not update as on the date of alleged accident. There is non compliance of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. Further stated that the rider/Petitioner was riding the two wheeler without valid driving license and vehicle documents and in a rash and negligent manner and had self fall and given false complaint against the driver of the vehicle belonging to the 2 nd respondent.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the Petitioner has relied upon the following decision: Misc. First Appeal No.388/2013 (MVSJ) : National Ins. Co. Ltd., Vs. Mallikarjuna. The counsel for the petitioner has reliedupon the decision Hence, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer and the Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the offending Tempo Traveler are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

7. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 20.06.2022 at about 10.00am, due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tempo Traveler bearing Reg.No.KA04C 9547 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?

The Respondent No.1 has denied the manner of accident and also denied the negligence and rash driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the self fall of the petitioner.
In the cross examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile showing the absence of negligence on the part of the driver of Tempo is elicited.

Therefore, on the basis of oral evidence of PW.1 and RW.1 and the police documents on record, the Tribunal holds that the accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Tempo Traveler bearing No.KA04C9547.

Monthly income:

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:

22. Issue No.4:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.6,42,600/ (Rupees Six Lakhs Forty Two Thousand and Six Hundred only) along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
